(R1 - Exparte  (R2 - By Sri.Sharanappa Gouda, Advocate  (R3 - Exparte  (R4 - By Smt.R.Sharadamba, Advocate) )
 JUDGMENT

This petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of M.V.Act, 1989 claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- in (SCCH-12) 3 MVC.No.281/2022 respect of injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic Accident.

2. In the petition it is stated that on 07.12.2021 at about 2.15pm, petitioner was proceeding in his Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MJ-9588 as a Driver from Nelamangala to his village by carefully observing all traffic rules and when he reached near Karekallu cross, Nelamangala-Kunigal NH-75 road, Bangalore district, at that time Breeza Car bearing No.KA- 05-MV-5804 came from backside of the petitioner, its driver drove the same in very high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's car from behind due to which, the petitioner car dashed to TATA lorry bearing No.RJ-27-GD-0741 which was parked on the road by its driver.
The said accident occurred only due to negligent driving and dangerous parking by the drivers of respondent no.1 and 3 respectively.

Petitioner's car crashed between these two respondents vehicle and petitioner sustained grievous injuries to left humerus fracture lower 1/3rd closed and comminuted proximal ulnar fracture, left radial head fracture and dislocation of right elbow joint, fracture and bleeding injuries all over the body.
3. That immediately he was shifted to Swasthya hospital, Nelamangala.
He was treated there as an inpatient and also continued follow up treatment.

He has spent Rs.4,00,000/- towards medical,
conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
He has to undergo further treatment and has to incur future medical expenses.
Prior to the date of accident, he was hale and healthy and earning Rs.15,000/- per month ad Driver.

Rakesha vs Praveen Karanika on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184632299/
2 (SCCH-12) 4 MVC.No.281/2022
Now he is suffering from disability and has lost future income and earning capacity.
He is also suffering pain and mental agony.

The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the drivers of Breeza Car bearing No.KA-05-MV-5804 and Tata Truck bearing No.RJ-27-GD-0741, Nelamangala Traffic police have registered a case in Crime No.448/2021 against the said drivers.
Therefore respondents no. 1 and 3 being owners of Car and Lorry and respondents no.2 and 4 being their insurance companies are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to petitioner.
On all these grounds he prayed to allow the petition and award compensation along with interest and costs in the above case.
4. On issuance of notice, respondent no.1 and 3 owner are served.
They remained absent on the date of hearing and hence, they are placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 and 4 insurance companies have appeared through their respective counsel and filed written statement separately.
5. Respondent No.2 insurance company contended that petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
It disputed the compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of IMV Act.
That petition is bad for non-joinder of proper and necessary parties as the insurer and insured of the car bearing reg.No.KA-51-MJ- 9588 are not made as parties.
Further he may be permitted to contest the claim petition under Sec.170 of M.V.Act.

That the car was not insured with this respondent as on the date of accident., There was no F.C to the car and the owner by allowing such a vehicle to ply on the road has violated the terms (SCCH-12) 5 MVC.No.281/2022 and conditions of the policy issued
and therefore this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.

As per the police documents, the alleged accident was occurred mainly due to the negligence of petitioner came to main road in a zig zag manner and without indiction without observing back coming vehicles took to left turn and dashed to stationed lorry which was moving on the left side of the main road and therefore the petitioner was 100% negligent in driving the vehicle.
At that time of accident the driver of the car and lorry were not possessing any driving license.
Age, occupation, income, and Loss of earning capacity of the petitioner are denied.
On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the petition.
6. Respondent No.4 insurance company filed written statement contending that petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
It stated that it has issued policy in respect of Tata lorry bearing No.RJ-27-GD-0741 and it is bounden duty of the petitioner to furnish the particulars of the policy.
Further it denied the manner of accident.

That petitioner was proceeding in car on NH75 and the said road is 30ft tar road and there is no hurdle to vehicle movements at a time 3 vehicles can move and petitioner who was driving the car suddenly slowed his speed without giving any signals and the driver of the car who was coming from back side went and dashed to the said car, petitioner without noticing the moving lorry he went and dashed to the rear portion of the lorry, the same is evidenced from police records.

That IMV report is concerned, it is clear that the lorry was damaged towards its rear door right side scratched (SCCH-12) 6 MVC.No.281/2022 and right side tail lamp scratched, this itself shows that the petitioner went and dashed to the said lorry.
That the Tata lorry was not parked on the high way without proper signals and indications.
Further its driver was not possessing valid D.L to drive the said class of vehicle, the 3rd respondent himself being owner and driver of the said vehicle has not taken caution to hold
D.L. Age, occupation and income of the petitioner are denied.
The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant without any legal basis.
Loss of earning capacity and financial loss of the petitioner are denied.

On all these grounds Rakesha vs Praveen Karanika on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184632299/
3
he prayed to dismiss the petition.

7. On the basis of above pleadings, I have framed the following:-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that the injuries shown in petition are sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident occurred on 07.12.2021 due to rash and negligent driving of driver of car bearing reg.No.KA- 05-MV-5804 when it hit him while he was traveling on car bearing No.KA-51MJ-9588 and due to the impact of the accident he dashed against the tata lorry bearing No.RJ- 27-GD-0741 which was allegedly parked on the road without any reflector near Karekally cross, Nelamangala-Kunigal NH-5 road, Bengaluru?
2. Whether the petitioner proves his age, occupation, income and permanent disability if any?
(SCCH-12) 7 MVC.No.281/2022 3. Whether the 2nd respondent proves occurred due tot he negligence of petitioner claimant?
4. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?

If so by whom and what is the quantum?
5. What Order or Award?
8. To prove his case, petitioner is examined as P.W.1.
Ex. P.1 to P.16
documents
are marked on his behalf.
Doctor by name S.A.Somashekara-Orthopaedic Surgeon of Victoria hospital, Bengaluru is examined as P.W.2 and through him Ex.
P.17 and 18 documents are marked.

On the other hand,
Administrative Officer of 4th respondent is examined as R.W.1.
Through him Ex.R.1 and 2 documents are marked.
The Legal Executive of respondent no.2 insurance company is examined as R.W.2.

Through him Ex.R.3 and 4 documents are marked and respondent evidence is cloased.
9.

On taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Tribunal and on hearing arguments, my answers to the above issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the Negative, Issue No.3: In the Negative, Issue No.4: Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.5: As per final order, for the following;
 (SCCH-12) 8 MVC.No.281/2022  REASONS Rakesha vs Praveen Karanika on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184632299/
4 10.
ISSUE NO.1 AND 3 : Since these issues are on the point of negligence and contributory negligence, they are taken together for discussion under common head.
To prove that he sustained injuries due to RTA dt.07.12.2021 petitioner himself entered witness box and got examined as P.W.1.
He reiterated petition averments in his chief examination.

He relied upon FIR, spot sketch, spot panchanama, complaint, IMV report, wound certificate, discharge summary with final report to prove that it was due to RTA he sustained injuries and RTA was caused due to negligence of drivers of Breeza car and lorry.
On the same day of the accident Nelamangala police have registered FIR in Crime No.448/2021 on the complaint given by petitioner herein which was recorded in the hospital.
His first information is regarding negligence of car and lorry drivers.
On the same day spot panchanama was drawn and sketch was prepared.
They show that it was highway.
It was 30ft wide road and all the vehicles went to left side edge of the road and there was entire road remaining to move ahead as it was one way.
As per the spot sketch all the 3 vehicles went on the left side edge of the road.
According to 4th respondent lorry was not parked and it was moving.
As per the IMV report damages to breeza car occurred on front left side which means it hit behind the petitioners car from the backside and petitioners car went and hit the lorry to its backside.
Even if the lorry was not in that spot, petitioners car would have hit something else due to the pressure created from the accident occurred to its backside.
Both lorry owner (SCCH-12) 9 MVC.No.281/2022 and car owner have not questioned the final report and FIR or any other police documents in which their involvement of their vehicle is found.
Both the insurance company authorized representatives have given evidence to the effect that, they were not negligent and other side vehicles were negligent.
Except the petitioner who was victim-cum-eye witness no other witnesses are examined to disprove the contention of the petitioner.
The evidence on record show that petitioner took left side after seeing the car coming in high speed behind him, but when the backside car hit him, he lost control and hit the front side lorry.
To show that lorry was moving and not parked, except the evidence of authorized representative of both respondents, no other evidence is available.
As per the final report and other police documents lorry was parked on the left side of the road without placing any reflectors or indicators.
Even petitioner stated that lorry was parked on the left side of the road without placing without any indicators.
This fact is not denied by the driver of the lorry or its owner.

Therefore, the available evidence on record clearly show that, driver of lorry had parked the vehicle without placing without any indicators and if the driver of breeza car had maintained the safe distance between his vehicle and the vehicle ahead, this accident could have been avoided.
Therefore, in the opinion of this court both the drivers of lorry and breeza car were negligent in their act.
11. 2nd respondent contended that petitioner himself was negligent.

To prove the said fact,
authorized representative of 2 nd respondent is examined as R.W.2.
He is not an eye witness to (SCCH-12) 10 MVC.No.281/2022 the incident and given evidence only on the basis of police documents.

His evidence weighed with the evidence of petitioner is victim-cum-eyewitness,
evidence of petitioner is more reliable and believable compared to the evidence of R.W.2.
In none of the documents produced by both side negligence on part of petitioner is found therefore, 2nd respondent has failed to prove that petitioner was negligent in driving the car.

On considering the entire evidence on record, the negligence on part of breeza car driver is more compared to the lorry driver, if the breeza car driver had not hit behind the petitioners car, petitioner could have moved Rakesha vs Praveen Karanika on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184632299/
5 easily and passed the lorry.
Only because car hit behind him, petitioner went and hit the lorry.

Accordingly, it is held that the driver of car bearing no.KA-05-MV-5804 was negligent to the extent of 80% and the driver of lorry was negligent to the extent of 20% and answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative and issue No.3 in the Negative.
12.
ISSUE NO.2 :
In respect of age, petitioner produced his aadhaar card at Ex.P.16 which shows that he was born on 26.02.1997, Accident took place on 07.12.2021.
He was aged 24 years at the time of accident.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner is considered as 24 years at the time of accident.
13. In the petition it is mentioned that he was Tractor driver earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
To prove his occupation and income no document is produced.
Hence, notional income has to be considered.
Accident being taken place in 2021 and he being resident of Bengaluru, considering cost of living, his income per month is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month.
In respect of permanent disability a doctor by name S.A.Somashekara, Orthopaedic Suyrgeon at Victoria hospital, Bengaluru is examined as P.W.2.
In his chief examination he stated that petitioner has sustained Humerus fracture lower 1/3rd, comminuted proximal ulna fracture, radial head fracture dislocation, elbow joint fracture.
Surgery was conducted in the form of ORIF with plating for fracture lower humerus and ORIF with plating for fracture proximal ulna left, IROF with TBW for fracture right olecranon.

Radiological examination revealed fractures of proximal ulna distal humerus left and right olecranon are united lateral with implants in situ, fracture site shows surgical scars over both upper limbs and deformity of right elbow is seen.
Petitioners complaints of pain and difficulty in using upper limbs for daily living , weight lifting and driving.
P.W.2 has assessed physical disability of both upper limb at 41.90% and 23% of whole body.
15. In the chief examination P.W.2 stated that petitioner is said to be a Tractor driver and the said disabilities will comes in the way of his driving profession.
Further he stated that he needs surgery for removal of implants at all 3 fracture sites which would cause around Rs.60,000/-.

Considering no driving licence produced by the petitioner to show that he was tractor driver and that his age being 24 years, chances of recovery being more, in the opinion of this court functional disability affecting the income of the petitioner is held as 15%.
Accordingly, I answer this issue Partly in the Affirmative.
(SCCH-12) 12 MVC.No.281/2022 16. ISSUE NO.4 :
In view of above reasons, injuries sustained by petitioner are due to the accident caused by the driver of the car and lorry mentioned above.
There is nexus between the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the accident.
Hence, he is entitled to compensation at the hands of respondents.
4th respondent insurance company has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of lorry.

2 nd respondent insurance company in written statement denies the issuance of insurance policy to the car at para 6, but in para 9 contended that, driver of the car violated the Rakesha vs Praveen Karanika on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184632299/
6 policy conditions.
Therefore, it has indirectly admitted issuance of policy to the breeza car.
Further it has produced copy of policy at Ex.R.4.
Hence, they have to indemnify the insured and liable to pay compensation to petitioner to the extent of the negligence.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under:
(i) Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.14.
Totally he has paid amount of Rs.2,68,192/- as per Ex.P.14 medical bills.
The said payment of bill is due to the accident caused to him.
They are subsequent to the date of accident.
Though they are disputed, no satisfactory material is placed to disbelieve the bills.
They are supported by Ex.P.13 prescriptions of the doctor.
Therefore, petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.2,68,192/-.
(ii) Food and nourishment:
The petitioner was admitted in Swasthya hospital from 07.12.2021 and discharged on 14.12.2021 and has produced discharge summary at Ex.P.12.
He was in hospital for 8 days.
Accident took place in the year (SCCH-12) 13 MVC.No.281/2022 2021.
Since he was in hospital, food and nourishment charges will have to be awarded.
Considering the cost of living, and food, nourishment charges if per day Rs.500/- is awarded it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence for food and nourishment Rs.500/- x 8 days = Rs.4,000/-is awarded.
(iii) Attendant charges:
For a period of inpatient for 8 days some one should have looked after petitioner in the hospital.
Even if his family member has taken care of him in the said period, that family member's income for those days is lost.
Hence per day if Rs.500/- is awarded as attendant charges in 2021, it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence for attendant charges Rs.500/- x 8 days =Rs.4,000/-is awarded.
(iv) Loss of income during laid up period:
As per the finding to issue No.2, the income of the petitioner per month is Rs.15,000/-.
He suffered 5 injuries which are grievous in nature.
He was inpatient for 8 days and he was advised to take rest.
Minimum 3 months is required to recover from such grievous injury.
Therefore, laid up period of petitioner is considered as total 3 months including in patient period and loss of income during laid up period is Rs.15,000/-x 3= Rs. 45,000/-
He is entitled to Rs.45,000/- as loss of income during laid up period.
(v) Conveyance charges:
It is stated that petitioner took treatment at Swasthya hospital.
He has spent money for conveyance for the purpose of treatment.

Hence, conveyance charges of Rs.5,000/-
is awarded.

(SCCH-12) 14 MVC.No.281/2022 (vi) Loss of future income due to Disability :
Rakesha vs Praveen Karanika on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184632299/
7

sentences.text: As per the findings given to issue no.2, there is functional disability of 15%.

Therefore, loss of future income due to disability is to be calculated as income per month Rs.15,000 X 12 months X 15%
disability X appropriate multiplier to the age group of 15-25 is 18.
Hence, in the opinion of this court, petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.4,86,000/- towards loss of future income due to disability.

(vii) For Future medical expenses: P.W.2 doctor who has assessed the disability of the petitioner has stated that petitioner needs to removal the implants which may require Rs.60,000/- but no estimation is produced.
In view of necessity of removal of implants for well being of the petitioner in the opinion of this court amount of Rs.25,000/- shall be awarded for future medical treatment.
Accordingly, Rs.25,000/- is awarded under this head.
(viii) For Pain and sufferings:
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries as per the wound certificate produced by him.
The records show that he underwent operation.
He was in hospital for 8 days and he underwent surgery therefore, he sustained pain and sufferings.
For pain and suffering the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- .
(ix) Physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life :

As per the evidence of treated doctor,
petitioner complained about difficulty in doing day to day work.
Difficulty in driving as he is a driver by profession.
He suffers discomfort.
Meaning, he cannot lead the normal life as he used to live before the (SCCH-12) 15 MVC.No.281/2022 accident.
Certainly accident has caused physical discomfort and come in the way of normal enjoyment of life.

Hence in the opinion of this court,
petitioner is entitled to compensation under the head of physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life.

Under the said head he is entitled for Rs.30,000/-
(x) Loss of future prospect:
As per the evidence of assessed doctor, petitioner complained about pain and restriction in movement but there is no specific evidence regarding future prospects loss of the petitioner.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under this head.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:-

iv. Loss of income during laid up 45,000/-

Therefore, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.9,17,192/- in respect of injuries sustained by him in the Road traffic accident.
As per the settled law interest @ 6% from the date of petition till the date of deposit will have to be awarded.
Accordingly, I answer this Issue "Partly in Affirmative".
17. ISSUE NO.5:
In view of the above reasons, I proceed to pass following :
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.9,17,192/- with interest @ 6% pa from the date of petition till the date of payment except future medical expenses of Rs.25,000/- .
The respondent no.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured and directed to deposit the 80% of the aforesaid months from the date of this order.
The respondent no.4 insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured and directed to deposit the 20% of the aforesaid (SCCH-12) 17 MVC.No.281/2022 months from the date of this order.

The petitioner is entitled to have release of 50% compensation and remaining 50%
shall be kept in F.D in the name of petitioner in any nationalized bank of his choice with a liberty to draw periodical interest.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.

Respondent No.2 and 4 insurance companies have appeared through their respective counsel and filed written statement separately.
5. Respondent No.2 insurance company contended that petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
It disputed the compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of IMV Act.
That petition is bad for non-joinder of proper and necessary parties as the insurer and insured of the car bearing reg.No.KA-51-MJ- 9588 are not made as parties.
Further he may be permitted to contest the claim petition under Sec.170 of M.V.Act.
That the car was not insured with this respondent as on the date of accident., There was no F.C to the car and the owner by allowing such a vehicle to ply on the road has violated the terms (SCCH-12) 5 MVC.No.281/2022 and conditions of the policy issued
and therefore this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
As per the police documents, the alleged accident was occurred mainly due to the negligence of petitioner came to main road in a zig zag manner and without indiction without observing back coming vehicles took to left turn and dashed to stationed lorry which was moving on the left side of the main road and therefore the petitioner was 100% negligent in driving the vehicle.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner proves that the injuries shown in petition are sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident occurred on 07.12.2021 due to rash and negligent driving of driver of car bearing reg.No.KA- 05-MV-5804 when it hit him while he was traveling on car bearing No.KA-51MJ-9588 and due to the impact of the accident he dashed against the tata lorry bearing No.RJ- 27-GD-0741 which was allegedly parked on the road without any reflector near Karekally cross, Nelamangala-Kunigal NH-5 road, Bengaluru?
2. Whether the petitioner proves his age, occupation, income and permanent disability if any?
(SCCH-12) 7 MVC.No.281/2022 3. Whether the 2nd respondent proves occurred due tot he negligence of petitioner claimant?
4. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so by whom and what is the quantum?
5. What Order or Award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In none of the documents produced by both side negligence on part of petitioner is found therefore, 2nd respondent has failed to prove that petitioner was negligent in driving the car.
There is nexus between the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the accident.
Hence, he is entitled to compensation at the hands of respondents.
For pain and suffering the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- .
(ix) Physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life :
As per the evidence of treated doctor,
petitioner complained about difficulty in doing day to day work.
Difficulty in driving as he is a driver by profession.
He suffers discomfort.
Meaning, he cannot lead the normal life as he used to live before the (SCCH-12) 15 MVC.No.281/2022 accident.
Certainly accident has caused physical discomfort and come in the way of normal enjoyment of life.
Hence in the opinion of this court,
petitioner is entitled to compensation under the head of physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Under the said head he is entitled for Rs.30,000/-
(x) Loss of future prospect:
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:-
Sl.No Particulars of Heads In Rs.
i. Medical expenses 2,68,192 /-
ii. Food and nourishment 4,000/-
iii. Attendant charges 4,000/-
iv. Loss of income during laid up 45,000/-
 period v. Conveyance charges 5,000/-
vi Loss of income due to disability 4,86,000/-
vii Future medical expenses 25,000/-
viii. Pain & Sufferings 50,000/-
Rakesha vs Praveen Karanika on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184632299/
8 ix.
Therefore, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.9,17,192/- in respect of injuries sustained by him in the Road traffic accident.
As per the settled law interest @ 6% from the date of petition till the date of deposit will have to be awarded.
Accordingly, I answer this Issue "Partly in Affirmative".
17. ISSUE NO.5:
In view of the above reasons, I proceed to pass following :
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.9,17,192/- with interest @ 6% pa from the date of petition till the date of payment except future medical expenses of Rs.25,000/- .
The respondent no.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured and directed to deposit the 80% of the aforesaid months from the date of this order.
The respondent no.4 insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured and directed to deposit the 20% of the aforesaid (SCCH-12) 17 MVC.No.281/2022 months from the date of this order.
The petitioner is entitled to have release of 50% compensation and remaining 50%
shall be kept in F.D in the name of petitioner in any nationalized bank of his choice with a liberty to draw periodical interest.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.
